items.title: Section: Why the Buddha Names Only Three Marks of the Conditioned, Not Four — Future, Past, and Present Each Get Their Own

items.zh: 問：若有為法，生、老、住、滅四有為相具足可得，何故世尊但說三種，一、生、二、滅、三、住異性？答：由一切行三世所顯故。從未來世本無而生。是故世尊由未來世，於有為法說生有為相。彼既生已落謝過去，是故世尊由過去世，於有為法說滅有為相。現在世法二相所顯，謂住及異。所以者何？唯現在時有住可得，前後變異亦唯現在。是故世尊由現在世，於有為法總說住、異為一有為相。問：佛聖弟子應觀有為具足三相，何故但說聖弟子眾於諸蘊中隨觀生滅而住，不說隨觀住異性耶？答：生及住異俱生所顯，是故二相合為一分，建立生品，即說隨觀一生相住；於第二分建立滅品，即說隨觀一滅相住。
items.en:
Second, explaining a further account; first, the three distinct marks; first, the question. Question: if conditioned phenomena fully possess four marks — arising, ageing, abiding, ceasing — why does the Blessed One teach only three: arising, ceasing, and abiding-with-difference? Second, the answer; first, the general statement. Answer: because all conditioned phenomena are revealed through the three time-periods.
Second, the two marks observed; first, the question. Question: since the Buddha's noble disciples should contemplate the conditioned as fully possessing three marks, why does scripture say only that noble disciples observe arising and ceasing with respect to the aggregates, without mentioning observation of abiding-with-difference? Second, the answer; first, clarifying the establishment. Answer: arising and abiding-with-difference are both revealed through arising, and so these two marks are combined into one category, establishing the class of arising, said to be observed as a single mark of arising abiding; a second category establishes the class of ceasing, said to be observed as a single mark of ceasing abiding.

items.title: Section: Why Impermanence Is Taught At All — And Mallikā's Unbroken Calm at News of Her Husband and Thirty-Two Sons

items.zh: 又若由此相起厭思惟，今於此中但說此相。謂於諸行中觀無常相，能起厭患、離欲、解脫，故但思惟無常性相。無常性相，本無今有、有已還無所顯。本無今有，是名為生；有已還無，是名為滅。
items.en:
Second, revealing impermanence; first, clarifying the purpose of this teaching; first, stating it. Since contemplating this mark gives rise to revulsion, only this mark is spoken of here. Second, explaining it. Observing the mark of impermanence within conditioned phenomena gives rise to revulsion, dispassion, and liberation — therefore one should reflect only on the nature and characteristics of impermanence.
Second, explaining the observed characteristic. The nature and characteristic of impermanence is revealed through what was originally absent and now exists, and what having existed then ceases to exist. Originally absent and now existing is called arising; having existed and then ceasing to exist is called cessation.

items.title: Section: Eleven Kinds of "Arising" Begin — From Moment-to-Moment Flux to the Nine Fetters Driving Rebirth

items.zh: 復次，生差別有多種。謂剎那生、相續生、增長生、心差別生、不可愛生、可愛生、下劣生、處中生、勝妙生、有上生、無上生。此中諸行剎那剎那新新而起，名剎那生。若具諸結、或不具結，從彼彼有情聚沒，往彼彼有情聚諸蘊續生，名相續生。若從嬰孩、童子等位，乃至往趣衰老等位，名增長生。若緣彼彼境界，於彼彼晝夜、彼彼剎那、臘縛牟呼栗多等位，數數遷謝，非一眾多種種心起，或樂相應、或苦相應、或不苦不樂相應，或有貪心、或離貪心，廣說乃至或善解脫心、或不善解脫心。如是名為心差別生。
items.en:
Third, extensively distinguishing them; first, distinctions in arising; first, stating and listing. Furthermore, the distinctions in arising are of many kinds: momentary arising, continuity arising, growth arising, arising through distinct mental states, undesirable arising, desirable arising, inferior arising, middling arising, excellent arising, arising with something superior remaining, and unsurpassed arising.
Second, explaining each; first, momentary arising. Here, conditioned phenomena arise ever anew, moment after moment; this is called momentary arising.
Second, continuity arising. Whether bound by the full range of fetters or only some, a being passes from one class of beings and, in another class of beings, its aggregates continue to arise; this is called continuity arising.
Third, growth arising. From the stages of infancy and childhood onward to the stage of ageing and decline, this is called growth arising.
Fourth, arising through distinct mental states. Encountering this or that object, throughout this or that day and night, this or that moment, minute, or hour, again and again shifting, not one but many different minds arise — joined with pleasure, joined with pain, joined with neither pleasure nor pain, with greed, free of greed, and so on in detail up through a well-liberated mind or a poorly liberated mind. This is called arising through distinct mental states.

items.title: Section: The Three Realms as Inferior, Middling, and Excellent Birth — and Four Levels of Awareness Entering the Womb

items.zh: 若那落迦、傍生、餓鬼苦趣中生，如是名為非可愛生。若於人天樂趣中生，名可愛生。若於下劣欲界中生，名下劣生。若於處中色界中生，名處中生。若於勝妙無色界生，名勝妙生。復有差別。謂最初入胎者，名下劣生；中二入胎者，名處中生；最後入胎者，名勝妙生。
items.en:
Fifth, undesirable arising. Rebirth in the hells, as an animal, or as a hungry ghost among the suffering destinies is called undesirable arising. Sixth, desirable arising. Rebirth among humans or in the pleasant destinies of the heavens is called desirable arising.
Seventh, inferior and other kinds of arising; first, distinguished by the three realms; first, inferior arising. Birth in the inferior desire realm is called inferior arising. Second, middling arising. Birth in the middling form realm is called middling arising. Third, excellent arising. Birth in the excellent formless realm is called excellent arising.
Second, distinguished by entering the womb. There is a further distinction: entering the womb with the least awareness is inferior arising; entering with an intermediate degree of the two forms of awareness is middling arising; entering with the fullest awareness is excellent arising.

items.title: Section: Completing Eleven Kinds of Arising — Cause and Result, Realm and Peak, Continuity and Its Final Cessation

items.zh: 復有差別。謂染污法及染污果生，名下劣生；若諸善法及善果生，名勝妙生；除善不善果無記法，所餘無記法生，名處中生。若依墮界生說，始從欲界乃至無所有處生，名有上生。非想非非想處生，名無上生。若依墮續生剎那相續生說，除阿羅漢等最後終位所有諸蘊，餘一切位所有行生，名有上生。若阿羅漢等最後終位所有行生，名無上生。
items.en:
There is a further distinction: birth from defiled phenomena together with a defiled resultant outflow is called inferior arising; birth from wholesome phenomena together with a wholesome resultant outflow is called excellent arising; birth from neutral phenomena, apart from wholesome or unwholesome ripened results, is called middling arising.
Eighth, arising with something superior remaining, and the rest; first, distinguished by realm and level; first, arising with something superior remaining. Following rebirth by realm, from the desire realm up through the sphere of nothingness, this is called arising with something superior remaining. Second, unsurpassed arising. Rebirth in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is called unsurpassed arising.
Second, distinguished by continuity; first, arising with something superior remaining. Following the continuity of rebirth and momentary continuity, apart from an arhat's aggregates at the very final stage, arising in every other stage is called arising with something superior remaining. Second, unsurpassed arising. An arhat's aggregates at the very final stage are called unsurpassed arising.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Ageing — the Body's Long Catalogue of Decline, and Why the Mind Alone Need Never Grow Old

items.zh: 復次，老差別當知亦有多種，所謂身老、心老、壽老、變壞老、自體轉變老。此中衰變等乃至身壞，廣說如經，是名身老。若樂受相應心變，苦受相應心轉；或善心變，染污心轉；或於可愛事中希望心變，希望不果心轉，是名心老。若於彼彼晝夜、彼彼剎那、臘縛、牟呼栗多等位，數數遷謝，壽量損少，漸漸轉減乃至都盡，是名壽老。若諸富貴興盛退失，無病色力充悅等變，名變壞老。若從善趣增盛聚中自體沒已，往於惡趣下劣聚中自體生起，名自體轉變老。復有
items.en:
Second, distinctions in ageing; first, explaining the names of these distinctions; first, stating and listing. Furthermore, the distinctions in ageing should be known to be of many kinds as well: bodily ageing, mental ageing, ageing of the lifespan, ageing through decline, and ageing through the transformation of one's own being.
Second, mental ageing. When a mind joined with pleasure shifts, and one joined with pain arises instead; or a wholesome mind shifts, and a defiled mind arises instead; or, regarding something desired, a hopeful mind shifts, and one whose hope is dashed arises instead — this is called mental ageing.
Third, ageing of the lifespan. Throughout this or that day and night, this or that moment, minute, or hour, again and again passing, one's remaining lifespan diminishes, gradually decreasing until fully exhausted — this is called ageing of the lifespan.
Fourth, ageing through decline. When wealth and flourishing reverse into decline, or freedom from illness and physical vigour and radiance change for the worse — this is called ageing through decline.
Fifth, ageing through the transformation of one's own being. When one's own being, from within a flourishing, favourable class of existence, ceases, and one's own being then arises within an inferior, unfavorable class of existence instead — this is called ageing through the transformation of one's own being.

blocks.text: The marks of conditioned things are explored in detail. One line is worth keeping: the body ages, but the mind need not.

"All phenomena are revealed through the three time-periods." Master Cháng Bǎi: arising concerns the future, going from non-existence to existence; ceasing concerns the past; abiding and change are already included in arising, for when a phenomenon appears it abides a moment and then changes.
Ru-Yi's heading recalls Mallikā, wife of the general Bandhula, whose calm held at news of the deaths of her husband and thirty-two sons: an example of one who has truly contemplated impermanence.

Phenomena arising anew moment after moment is momentary arising; passing from one class of beings to another is continuity arising. Master Cháng Bǎi: "fetter" is another name for affliction; it means joining with suffering.

Inferior desire realm, middling form realm, excellent formless realm. Master Cháng Bǎi: the formless realm is entirely a state of mind. On entering the womb, the "middle two" are wheel-turning kings, who enter knowingly, and pratyekabuddhas, who enter and dwell knowingly.
The peak is the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; the end of continuity is the arhat's final life.

Mental ageing: pleasure turning to pain, a wholesome mind turning defiled, hope turning to disappointment. Master Cháng Bǎi: only a turn from good to bad is called mental ageing. Ageing of the lifespan: it diminishes through days and nights until exhausted; a 臘縛 is about 1.6 minutes. Ageing of birth: ceasing in a good class and arising in a worse one.
If only a turn from good to bad counts as "mental ageing", then a mind that keeps turning towards the good does not age. Master Cháng Bǎi's reading is an encouragement for later life.

quiz.q: If four marks can be found, why does the Blessed One teach only three: arising, ceasing, and abiding-with-difference?
options: all phenomena are revealed through three time-periods: arising for the future, ceasing for the past, abiding-with-difference for the present
all phenomena are revealed through three realms: arising for the desire realm, abiding-with-difference for the form realm, ceasing for the formless realm
all are revealed through three feelings: arising for pleasant, ceasing for painful, abiding-with-difference for neutral
ageing is not a mark of the conditioned, so only three are taught
quiz.why: The treatise answers that all phenomena are revealed through the three time-periods. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha speaks of arising with regard to the future, going from non-existence to existence; of ceasing with regard to the past; and in the present, a phenomenon's appearing is abiding and its changing is difference.

quiz.q: Why does scripture say noble disciples observe only arising and ceasing, without mentioning abiding-with-difference?
options: abiding-with-difference is no mark of the conditioned, so it need not be observed
it is too subtle even for noble disciples to see
it belongs to the class of ceasing and is included in observing ceasing
arising and abiding-with-difference are both revealed through arising, so they are combined into one class of arising
quiz.why: The treatise combines arising and abiding-with-difference into the class of arising, with ceasing as the second class. Master Cháng Bǎi: abiding and difference are already included in arising, for when a phenomenon appears it abides for a moment and then changes.

quiz.q: How do momentary arising and continuity arising differ?
options: passing from one class of beings to another is momentary arising; arising each moment is continuity arising
infancy through old age is continuity arising; passing between classes is momentary arising
phenomena arising ever anew each moment is momentary arising; passing from one class of beings with aggregates continuing in another is continuity arising
the many minds arising are momentary arising; aggregates continuing are growth arising
quiz.why: The treatise calls phenomena arising ever anew, moment after moment, momentary arising, and passing from one class of beings with the aggregates continuing in another, continuity arising. Master Cháng Bǎi: after dying within one class, with afflictions as cause, one is born again in another class.

quiz.q: What are the "fetters" in "whether bound by the full range of fetters or only some"?
options: another name for karma, meaning that which brings results
another name for affliction, meaning that which joins one with suffering
another name for precepts, meaning that which restrains body and mind from heedlessness
another name for seeds, meaning that which stores phenomena
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: fetter is another name for affliction, and its meaning is joining with suffering. Whether beings have all the fetters or only some, they pass from one class of beings and are reborn in another.

quiz.q: By the three realms, how are inferior, middling, and excellent arising assigned?
options: the form realm inferior, the desire realm middling, the formless realm excellent
the three evil destinies inferior, humans middling, the gods excellent
the desire realm inferior, the form realm middling, the formless realm excellent
the desire realm inferior, the formless realm middling, the form realm excellent
quiz.why: The treatise assigns the inferior desire realm, the middling form realm, and the excellent formless realm in that order. Master Cháng Bǎi says of the formless realm that it is entirely a state of mind, without the coarse obstruction of form. The destinies are used for desirable and undesirable arising, not here.

quiz.q: The English reads 中二入胎 as "an intermediate degree of the two forms of awareness." What does 中二 actually refer to?
options: those whose awareness is half clear and half unclear
the middle two of the four kinds of womb-entry, wheel-turning kings and pratyekabuddhas, not a degree of awareness
the two stages of entering and dwelling, both with moderate awareness
the intermediate state and womb-entry, hence "middle two"
quiz.why: The Sub-commentary and Master Cháng Bǎi read this through the four kinds of womb-entry in the Mind Ground: "middle two" means wheel-turning kings, who enter knowingly only, and pratyekabuddhas, who enter and dwell knowingly. The English turns this into a degree of awareness, and "least" and "fullest" likewise replace the terms first and last.

quiz.q: The English uses "unsurpassed" for two cases. What are they by realm and by continuity, and what does "unsurpassed" mean?
options: by realm, the buddha ground; by continuity, a bodhisattva's last body; in both, the most excellent among all beings, whom none can equal
by realm, the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; by continuity, an arhat's very last stage; in both, nothing further lies beyond
by realm, Brahmā's heaven; by continuity, a wheel-turning king; in both, the highest in the world
by realm, the sphere of nothingness; by continuity, stream-entry; in both, the abode of noble ones
quiz.why: By realm the treatise means the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the peak of the three existences; by continuity it means the conditioned arising at an arhat's final stage. Master Cháng Bǎi explains the second by whether a further body of the five aggregates will continue. So "unsurpassed" means nothing further, not "best."

quiz.q: What, according to Master Cháng Bǎi, is the distinguishing feature of "mental ageing"?
options: only a turn from good to bad counts as mental ageing, as when hope turns to hopelessness
any change of thought whatever, whether from bad to good or good to bad, counts as mental ageing
a turn from bad to good counts as mental ageing
memory fading with the years counts as mental ageing
quiz.why: The treatise lists pleasure turning to pain, a wholesome mind turning defiled, and hope turning to dashed hope. Master Cháng Bǎi: mental ageing has one distinguishing feature, that only a turn from good to bad is called mental ageing; what was hopeful becoming hopeless is mental ageing.

quiz.q: The English gives "moment, minute, or hour" for 剎那、臘縛、牟呼栗多. By the reckoning the lecture cites, how long are these units, and which ageing does the passage describe?
options: one 牟呼栗多 is forty-eight minutes and thirty 臘縛 make one, so the English is only approximate; this is ageing of the lifespan
one 牟呼栗多 is sixty minutes and sixty 臘縛 make one, so the English is exact; this is ageing of the lifespan
one 牟呼栗多 is forty-eight minutes and thirty 臘縛 make one, so the English is only approximate; this is ageing through decline
one 牟呼栗多 is a full day and night, so the English is far too short; this is bodily ageing
quiz.why: The treatise says the lifespan diminishes through days, nights, and these units of time until exhausted, which is ageing of the lifespan. The lecture cites the Sarvāstivāda reckoning: thirty 臘縛 make one 牟呼栗多, which is forty-eight minutes, so a 臘縛 is about 1.6 minutes. The English "minute" and "hour" are therefore only rough equivalents.

quiz.q: What is "ageing through the transformation of one's own being"?
options: wealth and flourishing declining, vigour and radiance changing for the worse
a mind joined with pleasure shifting to one joined with pain
passing again and again, the lifespan decreasing until exhausted
ceasing in a flourishing, favourable class of existence and arising in an inferior, unfavorable one
quiz.why: The treatise defines it as one's own being ceasing in a flourishing, favourable class and arising in an inferior one. Master Cháng Bǎi: a life going from the good destinies of humans and gods, even from the form and formless heavens, to birth in the three evil paths. The other options are ageing through decline, mental ageing, and ageing of the lifespan.
